# Best portable power station for camping

The right pick depends on how much you need to run. Most weekend campers do well with a small 250-500Wh unit. Bigger trips or a 12V fridge call for a 1kWh+ model.

## Light weekend trips (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
| Pick | Capacity / Output | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | 288Wh / 300W, 8.3 lb | ~$249 | Top overall pick on PowerStationGearLab. Jackery has replaced it with the 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold on Amazon. |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | 288Wh / 300W, 9.3 lb | ~$199 | Built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the AC-outlet version, not the "DC" variant. |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | 286Wh / 600W, 9.9 lb | ~$269-299 | Twice the inverter power of the Jackery, and expandable to 572Wh. |
| **Bluetti EB3A** | 268Wh / 600W, 10.1 lb | ~$179 | Cheapest real LiFePO4 option. |

All four are on the [PowerStationGearLab camping guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), which has the Amazon buy buttons. That site earns affiliate commissions. OutdoorGearLab scored the Jackery 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low in its lab tests, so treat these as budget convenience picks rather than top performers.

## Multi-day trips, a fridge, or tools
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It has 2,042Wh, 2,200W output, weighs 39 lb, and scored 81. It's listed at $1,499 but was reported under $900 on Amazon. It can't run a space heater or electric burner for long. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is the best value, at about $530 on sale. It has 1,800W output and weighs 25 lb. The fan is noisy and capacity is limited. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's best for camping. It has 1,536Wh, is IP65-rated, weighs just under 40 lb, and costs $1,079 at 10% off on Amazon. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is TechRadar's camping pick, at about $799 per PowerStationGearLab. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))

## Mid-size option with a direct buy link
The **Bluetti AC180** has 1,152Wh of LiFePO4, 1,800W output, and weighs about 16 kg (35 lb). It has a 5-year warranty and takes up to 500W of solar input. It's $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the listing says it tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. It has no expansion port, and the $599 option is a bundle with a 100W solar panel.
[Buy at BLUETTI's official US store](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, and Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Details are on the [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180).

## My suggestion
- **Tent or car camping for a weekend:** the Anker SOLIX C300 or Jackery 300 Plus.
- **Fridge, tools, or a few nights off-grid:** the Anker C1000 Gen 2 for price, or the Jackery 2000 v2 for capacity.

Prices change often, and a major sales period around Black Friday is coming up, so check the current price before buying. I couldn't verify direct retailer links for the non-Bluetti models, so use the "Check price" buttons on the review pages above.

If you tell me what you'll power (CPAP, fridge, e-bike) and how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
